paragraphs: The Discovery TDV8 uses the 4.4-litre V8 diesel engine, fitted across the D3 and D4 generations from 2004 to 2016. It shares its fundamental architecture with the TDV6/SDV6 family, with the same timing chain, injector seal, and EGR components — just in a V8 configuration with four extra cylinders. The TDV8 was positioned as the range-topping diesel option during this era, offering more power and torque than its V6 stablemates. If you have a Discovery with the TDV8 badge, the engine's known wear patterns are well understood at this point — and we know exactly what to address during a rebuild. Land Rover Discovery TDV8 Engine Compatibility Because the Discovery TDV8 spans two generations (D3 and D4) with running changes between them, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming parts are interchangeable across all years — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact year and generation (D3/L319 or D4/L319 facelift) - Drivetrain and ancillary specification - Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic TDV8 quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual vehicle. cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the Discovery TDV8 from 2023 to present. The engine features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older engine V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every engine rebuild.
